Assemble brms priors from app-level inputs

Source: R/utils-priors.R
assemble_brms_priors.Rd

Internal helper that builds a named list of brms prior strings based on the chosen prior type, family, and adaptive prior recommendations.

Usage

assemble_brms_priors(
  prior_type,
  prior_effect_mean,
  prior_effect_sd,
  heterogeneous_variance,
  model_family_value,
  adaptive_priors,
  treatment_coef = NULL,
  has_random_slope = FALSE,
  formula_str = NULL
)

Arguments

prior_type

Character: "default", "informative", "meta_analytic", or "sensitivity". The informative prior is normal with SD equal to half the adaptive weakly-informative SD, centered on prior_effect_mean when that is a finite number and on 0 otherwise. The sensitivity (diffuse) prior doubles the adaptive SD (5 outcome SDs on identity links, 5 on log/logit links), so it is never narrower than the default, and doubles the session-slope priors of formula_str by the same factor; comparing the two is the prior sensitivity analysis. "sensitivity" returns only this diffuse arm: the default arm is the "default" type, and run_sensitivity_analysis() fits the arms and compares them.

prior_effect_mean

Numeric mean of the elicited treatment prior, used by the meta-analytic and informative types.

prior_effect_sd

Numeric SD for the meta-analytic prior; must be positive and finite (an error otherwise).

heterogeneous_variance

Logical; if TRUE add separate sigma priors.

model_family_value

Character name of the brms family.

adaptive_priors

List from generate_adaptive_priors().

treatment_coef

Optional name of the treatment coefficient. When supplied with an informative or meta-analytic prior type, the elicited treatment prior targets only this coefficient (coef) and a weakly-informative default covers the remaining b coefficients. When NULL with those types, a warning is issued: the elicited mean cannot be applied and the treatment SD falls on the whole b class with mean 0.

has_random_slope

Logical; used only without formula_str: if TRUE an lkj(2) prior is emitted on the correlation (cor) parameter. With formula_str, the cor prior is emitted only when a single-bar group term such as (1 + level_AB | case) has two or more coefficients; uncorrelated || terms and one-coefficient terms have no correlation, and brms errors on a prior that matches no parameter.

formula_str

Optional model formula string. When supplied, each session-count term of the formula (time_*, trend_*) with a scale in adaptive_priors$slopes gets its own normal(0, scale) prior (see generate_adaptive_priors()).

Value

Named list of prior specifications with attributes.

Details

With heterogeneous_variance = TRUE the log-scale residual SD intercept is normal(log pooled within-phase SD, 1) and the phase contrasts on it normal(0, 1) (see generate_adaptive_priors()). Shape (negative binomial, Gamma), precision (beta), and degrees-of-freedom (Student-t) parameters keep the brms defaults. Default priors have limited influence in larger samples, not with a few cases; compare a second shape or precision prior in the sensitivity analysis (see recommendations$dispersion of generate_adaptive_priors()).

With an elicited (informative or meta-analytic) prior on treatment_coef, the remaining b coefficients get a class-level default prior. When formula_str is given and every fixed term already has its own prior, that class-level prior is dropped, since brms warns about a prior that matches no parameter.
